Relocation Advisory Assistance personnel will have listings of available homes, apartments, and business locations to aid those people who are displaced to obtain new living or business locations.
In addition, they will be at the property owner's disposal to aid in the selection of alternate locations and to assist in completing forms necessary for receiving the moving and supplemental payments.
The Federal Highway Act of 1968 provides a new and more liberal compensation for families displaced by highway construction. All displaced persons will be compensated for moving expenses. Owner-occupants of single, two or three family dwellings whose homes are acquired can receive a payment to purchase a comparable property, and will be advised of the amount of the supplemental payment at the commencement of negotiations. An amendment to the Illinois Highway Code, approved September 17, 1971, allows a payment of up to $15,000.00 for this purpose.
Families who rent can receive a rent supplement of up to $4,000.00 when a dwelling unit comparable to the one displaced has a higher rental. A family could choose to apply the entire amount up to a maximum of $4,000.00 as a down payment for purchasing a new home.
H. Conservation
In view of the urban nature of the area, the proposed improvement is not expected to have significant effects on conservational values.
Some benefits to the area may result from the improvement since the proposed enclosed drainage system would reduce erosion and sedimentation in the present open ditches.
The protection and preservation of any aboriginal records, antiquities or artifacts encountered in the implementation of the proposed project will be in accordance with current policies and procedures of the Federal Highway Administration concerning archaeological and paleontological salvage as well as the "Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction".
